errors.english: From these words that are worth grasping and venerable words, it emerges with certainty in order to exhaust suffering.
errors.why: ནས here abbreviates the list ('...worthy words, venerable words, up to: [speech] that leads to deliverance for the exhaustion of suffering'), not a source 'from these words'.

note: Faithful rendering of the list of eloquences and the epithets of the Lord of Speech; one list-abbreviation misread as an ablative.
The syllogism, its application to members, and the opponent's charge of an unestablished reason are rendered accurately.

errors.english: one can walk a hundred yojanas and back
errors.why: The Tibetan says a hundred thousand yojanas (brgya stong).

fix.find: one can walk a hundred yojanas and back
fix.replace: one can travel a hundred thousand yojanas and return

errors.english: recites the vidyāmantra one hundred thousand times at the door of the house
errors.why: The number of recitations is eight thousand (stong phrag brgyad), not one hundred thousand.

fix.find: recites the vidyāmantra one hundred thousand times at the door of the house
fix.replace: recites the vidyāmantra eight thousand times at the door of the house

errors.english: If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, the target will be afflicted with leprosy.
errors.why: The Tibetan has two rice-flour effigy rites: the first paralyses the enemy, the second causes leprosy; the paralysis rite is dropped.

fix.find: If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, the target will be afflicted with leprosy.
fix.replace: If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, the enemy will become paralyzed. If one makes an effigy from rice flour and smears it with the powder, the target will be afflicted with leprosy.

errors.english: one will be separated from that enemy
errors.why: The effect is that the enemies are divided (set at odds), not that the practitioner is separated from the enemy.

fix.find: one will be separated from that enemy
fix.replace: the enemies will be split apart

errors.english: If one gives the powder to an enemy,
errors.why: The powder is first mixed with excrement before being given to the enemy.

fix.find: If one gives the powder to an enemy,
fix.replace: If one mixes the powder with excrement and gives it to an enemy,

note: Generally follows the rites, but two numbers are wrong, one rite and one ingredient are dropped, and one effect is misassigned.

errors.english: Not only is this translated here
errors.why: འགྱུར here means the offense 'occurs/becomes', not 'is translated'.
'The following training rules' heads the list, of which 'threatening [with a raised hand]' is the first item; it is not 'threatening a training rule'.
gnas ngan len is Skt. dauṣṭhulya; 'sanghadisesa' is the Pali form, not the Sanskrit (saṅghāvaśeṣa) of this Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition.

errors.english: refers to the intention to strike another person
errors.why: The commentary says the 'other' thing to be struck is the mind (one's own disturbed mind), not another person; the rule is about not striking one's own body.

fix.find: refers to the intention to strike another person
fix.replace: refers to the mind being what is to be struck

note: Offense counting is clear, but the gloss on 'the object to be struck is another' is inverted and the opening and the list of rules are garbled.

errors.english: should the value of each owner's property be calculated individually to see if it meets the threshold
errors.why: The commentary rules that each owner's property is counted separately (glossing 'their individual shares'); it is a ruling, not an open question.
The one who dies is the fully ordained monk (dge slong) included in the count, not a novice.

errors.english: If a monk steals those goods from a separate building and moves them
errors.why: The monk takes goods dedicated to one building and moves them to a separate building, not from one.

note: Follows the Vinaya argument broadly, but turns a ruling into a question, calls the monk a novice, and reverses the direction of the misappropriation.

errors.english: Then, having understood that this is difficult to find, the Blessed One spoke to the retinue
errors.why: The thought 'this is hard to find' belongs to the retinue, who became faithful and inspired; the Blessed One knew this about them.

note: Verses on the cakras and the two stages and the commentary on the Hevajra opening are rendered soundly.
The cosmological description of the golden mountains, with all distances and heights, is accurate.

errors.english: It is stated that in the state of being with stains, one does not dwell in a manner of apprehending for the sake of being afflicted
errors.why: The single negation governs the whole list: enlightenment does not abide by way of apprehension for accumulating virtue, diminishing faults, etc.; the English presents the earlier purposes as positive statements and changes the subject to 'one'.

errors.english: the Bodhisattva [note: a being dedicated to attaining enlightenment for the benefit of all] also attains the state of all-knowingness
errors.why: The sentence continues on the next side with མི་ནུས: a bodhisattva with dualistically apprehended roots of virtue is unable to attain omniscience; the English closes it as an assertion.

note: The three-nature etymologies are good, but the negated list on apprehension and the closing sentence are misconstrued.

errors.english: so too is the aspect non-distinct from the manifestation
errors.why: The predicate carried over is 'diverse': likewise the aspect that is non-distinct from the manifestations is also diverse.

note: A difficult Pramāṇa sub-commentary followed closely; one conclusion loses its predicate.

errors.why: ye shes is gnosis/wisdom (jñāna), not faith.

note: The ultimate/relative bodhicitta exegesis and the dharmakāya/sambhogakāya mapping are rendered well apart from one term.
